name: Tsaang Gubat (TL)
shortDescription: Isang halamang palaging luntian na katutubo sa Pilipinas at iba pang bahagi ng Asya. Ang mga dahon nito ay napatunayang may bisa laban sa pagtatae, pananakit, at mikrobyo. Isa ito sa 10 halamang gamot na ineendorso ng DOH at ginawa nang aprubadong tableta para sa pananakit ng tiyan.

preparation.description: Boil 5–6 fresh leaves in 2 cups of water for 10 minutes. Strain and drink while warm.
Crush fresh leaves into a paste and apply directly to the affected area.
Tsaang gubat tablet has been formulated and registered with the Philippine Food and Drug Administration (FDA) after Phase I–III clinical trials. Listed in the Philippine National Formulary.

facts.habitat: Tropical lowland forests; grows wild in disturbed areas and open fields

warnings: Consult a doctor before using for medicinal purposes.
Do not consume in excessive amounts.
Avoid use if allergic to plants in the Boraginaceae family.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women should consult a healthcare professional before use.
Not a substitute for professional medical treatment.

cultivationGuide.soil: Well-drained, loamy to sandy soil; tolerates poor soil
cultivationGuide.sunlight: Full sun to partial shade (4–6 hours daily)
cultivationGuide.growthTime: 1–2 years to reach usable size; shrub matures at 1.5–4 meters
tips: Prune regularly to encourage bushy growth.
Harvest leaves before flowering for highest potency.
Can be grown as a hedge or ornamental shrub.

research.title: Evaluation of the bioactivity of triterpene mixture isolated from Carmona retusa (Vahl.) Masam leaves
research.summary: The major constituent of C. retusa leaves is a triterpene mixture (α-amyrin, β-amyrin, and bauerenol). At 100 mg/kg, the triterpene mixture exhibited 51% analgesic activity and 29% anti-diarrheal activity (charcoal tracing test), which increased to 55% at 250 mg/kg. The triterpene mixture showed moderate antimicrobial activity against S. aureus, C. albicans, and T. mentagrophytes. Results were comparable to mefenamic acid (a commercial NSAID) at α = 0.01.
research.reference: Villaseñor IM, Canlas AP, Faustino KM, Plana KG. J Ethnopharmacol. 2004 May;92(1):53–6. DOI: 10.1016/j.jep.2004.01.017

research.title: Ehretia microphylla Tablet Formulation for Biliary and Gastrointestinal Colic: A Review of its Phytochemical Constituents, Pharmacologic Activities and Clinical Researches
research.summary: Comprehensive review of tsaang gubat's phytochemical constituents (flavonoids, phenolics, triterpenes, alkaloids) and pharmacologic activities (antibacterial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, anti-diarrheal, anti-angiogenesis, wound healing, anti-cancer). The tsaang gubat tablet has been granted a full patent and is registered with the Philippine FDA. It is listed in the Philippine National Formulary after Phase I–III clinical trials.
research.reference: Legaspi CLB, Bagaoisan DM. Acta Medica Philippina. 2020 Feb;54(1):80–85. DOI: 10.47895/amp.v54i1.1108

research.title: Ehretia genus: a comprehensive review of its botany, ethnomedicinal uses, phytochemistry, and pharmacology
research.summary: Comprehensive review of the Ehretia genus covering botany, ethnomedicinal uses, phytochemistry, and pharmacology. Confirms anti-diarrheal, anti-inflammatory, analgesic, antibacterial, and antioxidant properties of E. microphylla. Identifies key bioactive compounds including triterpenes and rosmarinic acid.
research.reference: Jiang S et al. Frontiers in Pharmacology. 2025. DOI: 10.3389/fphar.2025.1526359

comparisonTraits.leaf: Small, rounded, obovate leaves approximately 1–2.5 cm in length with lobed apex and short bristly hairs
comparisonTraits.flower: Small white flowers, axillary, solitary or in pairs on a slender hairy peduncle
comparisonTraits.stem: Highly branched, divaricate with brown bark approximately 3 mm thick
comparisonTraits.smell: Mild, herbal tea-like scent when leaves are crushed

name: Tawa-tawa (TL)
shortDescription: Isang taunang damo na malawak na nakakalat sa mga tropikal na rehiyon kabilang ang Pilipinas. Kilala sa tradisyonal na paggamit sa pamamahala ng dengue fever. Ipinakita ng mga klinikal na pag-aaral na nakakatulong itong mapataas ang bilang ng platelet.

preparation.description: Boil 1 cup of fresh whole plant (roots, stems, leaves) in 2 cups of water for 15 minutes. Strain and drink warm, 1 cup 3 times daily.
Crush fresh leaves and apply as a paste to cuts, wounds, and skin irritations.
Steep dried aerial parts in hot water for 10 minutes. Strain and drink.

facts.origin: Tropical Americas; naturalized worldwide in tropical regions
facts.habitat: Waste places, roadsides, lawns, and disturbed areas in tropical regions

warnings: Consult a doctor before using for medicinal purposes, especially for dengue.
Do not consume in excessive amounts; the plant contains latex which can be irritating.
Avoid contact with latex sap — it may cause skin and eye irritation.
Not a substitute for professional medical treatment for dengue fever.
Pregnant women should avoid use due to potential uterine stimulant effects.
Euphorbia hirta should not be the sole treatment for severe thrombocytopenia.

cultivationGuide.soil: Adaptable; grows in sandy, loamy, and clay soils; tolerates poor soil
tips: Grows readily as a weed; collect from open fields or grow in a garden pot.
Harvest the whole plant when flowering for maximum potency.
No special fertilization needed.

research.title: Management of thrombocytopenia and flu-like symptoms in dengue patients with herbal water of Euphorbia hirta
research.summary: A clinical study of 125 dengue patients showed that over 70% of patients had improvement in platelet count, white blood cell count, fever, and flu-like symptoms after consuming herbal water of E. hirta. Leucopoenia improved significantly after use of the aqueous extract.
research.reference: Mir M, Khurshid R, Aftab R. J Ayub Med Coll Abbottabad. 2012 Jul-Dec;24(3-4):6–9. PMID: 24669596

research.title: Potential Use of Euphorbia hirta for Dengue: A Systematic Review of Scientific Evidence
research.summary: Systematic review confirming that E. hirta has significantly increased platelet counts in both animal models and clinical studies of dengue patients. Mean platelet count was increased by 80% following E. hirta treatment for 9 days in one clinical study. The plant shows promise as a complementary treatment for dengue.
research.reference: Perera SD, Kumarasinghe G, Abeysinghe M. Evid Based Complement Alternat Med. 2018. DOI: 10.1155/2018/2048530

research.title: Euphorbia hirta: Its chemistry, traditional and medicinal uses, and pharmacological activities
research.summary: Comprehensive review (cited 479 times) covering the chemistry, traditional uses, and pharmacological activities of E. hirta. Confirmed antimicrobial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antidiarrheal, anti-asthmatic, and antiviral properties. Key phytochemicals include quercetin, gallic acid, tannins, and flavonoids.
research.reference: Kumar S, Malhotra R, Kumar D. Pharmacogn Rev. 2010;4(8):174–184. DOI: 10.4103/0973-7847.70915

comparisonTraits.leaf: Small, hairy, oblong leaves with a reddish-purple center spot, arranged oppositely on hairy stems
comparisonTraits.flower: Tiny reddish flowers clustered in the leaf axils
comparisonTraits.stem: Hairy, prostrate or erect stems that exude milky latex when broken

name: Oregano (TL)
shortDescription: Isang halamang may makapal at mabangong mga dahon, malawakang ginagamit sa tradisyonal na panggagamot. Napatunayang may matapang na katangiang laban sa mikrobyo, pamamaga, at nakatutulong sa paghilom ng sugat.

preparation.description: Boil 5–6 fresh leaves in 1 cup of water for 5–10 minutes. Strain and drink warm. For children, add honey.
Crush fresh leaves and extract juice. Mix with honey for a soothing cough syrup. Take 1 teaspoon 2–3 times daily.
Crush fresh leaves into a paste and apply to the affected area for insect bites, rashes, or minor wounds.

facts.origin: Native to Southern and Eastern Africa; naturalized throughout the tropics
facts.habitat: Tropical and subtropical gardens; thrives in warm, dry conditions

warnings: Consult a doctor before using for medicinal purposes.
Do not consume essential oil directly — it is highly concentrated.
May cause allergic reactions in some individuals.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women should consult a healthcare professional before use.
Avoid prolonged use of essential oil on skin without dilution.

cultivationGuide.soil: Well-drained, sandy to loamy soil; tolerates drought
cultivationGuide.sunlight: Full sun to partial shade (6 hours daily)
cultivationGuide.watering: Water moderately; allow soil to dry between waterings (succulent plant)
cultivationGuide.growthTime: Rapid growth; harvestable in 4–6 weeks from cuttings
tips: Very easy to grow from stem cuttings in pots or garden beds.
Prune regularly to encourage bushy growth.
Can be grown indoors near a sunny window.
Drought-tolerant — avoid overwatering.

research.title: Plectranthus amboinicus (Lour.) Spreng: A multi therapeutic agent — A review
research.summary: Comprehensive review (cited 519 times) confirming numerous pharmacological properties including antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, antitumor, wound healing, anti-epileptic, larvicidal, and antidiabetic activities. The essential oil is rich in carvacrol and thymol, potent antimicrobial and antioxidant compounds.
research.reference: Arumugam G, Manjula S, Paari K. Biomed Pharmacother. 2016;84:341–349. DOI: 10.1016/j.biopha.2016.09.006. PMC6274163

research.title: Plectranthus amboinicus: A Systematic Review of Traditional Uses, Phytochemical Properties, and Therapeutic Applications
research.summary: Systematic review confirming significant antimicrobial activity of P. amboinicus extracts and essential oils against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, notable antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, and wound healing properties. Validates diverse therapeutic potential across infectious diseases, oncology, and wound care.
research.reference: Filipe MS, Bangay G, Brauning FZ et al. Pharmaceuticals (MDPI). 2025;18(5):707. DOI: 10.3390/ph18050707

research.title: Evaluation of the Effect of Plectranthus amboinicus L. Leaf Extracts on the Bacterial Antioxidant System and Cell Membrane Integrity of Pseudomonas aeruginosa PA01
research.summary: Study demonstrated that P. amboinicus leaf extracts disrupt the bacterial antioxidant system and compromise cell membrane integrity of P. aeruginosa, confirming its potent antimicrobial mechanism of action.
research.reference: Sawant S, Baldwin TC, Metryka O, Rahman A. Pathogens. 2023;12(6):853. DOI: 10.3390/pathogens12060853

comparisonTraits.leaf: Thick, succulent, oval-shaped leaves with scalloped edges; covered in fine hairs; strongly aromatic
comparisonTraits.flower: Small pale blue-purple flowers in loose spikes
comparisonTraits.stem: Fleshy, square cross-section (characteristic of Lamiaceae), green to purplish
comparisonTraits.smell: Strong, pungent oregano-like aroma when leaves are crushed (due to carvacrol and thymol)

name: Mangga (TL)
shortDescription: Isang malawakang itinatanim na tropikal na puno na ang mga dahon, balat ng kahoy, at prutas ay nagtataglay ng mangiferin at iba pang mga sangkap na may napatunayang katangiang laban sa diabetes, pamamaga, at nakakabuti sa puso.

preparation.description: Boil 5–10 fresh or dried mango leaves in 2 cups of water for 15 minutes. Strain and drink warm, 1–2 times daily.
Crush fresh bark into a paste and apply to the affected area.
Eat ripe mango fruit fresh for nutritional benefits. Rich in vitamins A, C, and fiber.

facts.origin: South Asia (India, Myanmar, Bangladesh); widely cultivated in tropical regions
facts.habitat: Tropical and subtropical regions; thrives in warm, humid climates

warnings: Mango sap and peel can cause contact dermatitis (allergic skin reaction) in sensitive individuals.
People with latex allergy may also be allergic to mango.
Mango leaves are not a substitute for prescribed diabetes medication.
Consult a doctor before using mango leaf decoction for medicinal purposes.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women should consult a healthcare professional before use.

cultivationGuide.soil: Deep, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil (pH 5.5–7.5)
cultivationGuide.watering: Regular watering for young trees; mature trees are drought-tolerant
cultivationGuide.growthTime: 3–6 years from grafting; 8–10 years from seed to bear fruit
tips: Protect young trees from frost.
Prune to shape the canopy and improve air circulation.
Apply balanced fertilizer before flowering and after fruit harvest.
Bag fruits on the tree to protect from pests.

research.title: Mangifera indica (Mango)
research.summary: Comprehensive review (cited 690 times) documenting mango's antidiabetic, antioxidant, anti-viral, cardiotonic, hypotensive, and anti-inflammatory properties. Mangiferin, a polyphenolic antioxidant and glucosyl xanthone, is identified as a key bioactive compound responsible for many of these effects.
research.reference: Shah KA, Patel MB, Patel RJ, Parmar PK. Pharmacogn Rev. 2010;4(8):112–118. DOI: 10.4103/0973-7847.70910. PMC3249901

research.title: Multifaceted Health Benefits of Mangifera indica L. (Mango): The Fruit That Should Be Included in Everyone's Diet
research.summary: Review (cited 302 times) providing an overview of the antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer properties of mango. Confirms that mango extracts reduce oxidative stress, inflammation, and cancer cell proliferation through mangiferin and other polyphenols.
research.reference: Lauricella M, Emanuele S, Di Sano C et al. Nutrients. 2017;9(5):525. DOI: 10.3390/nu9050525

research.title: A Review on Ethnopharmacological Applications, Pharmacological Activities, and Phytochemical Composition of Mangifera indica
research.summary: Review (cited 318 times) documenting the ethnopharmacological applications and pharmacological activities of M. indica, including antidiabetic, antioxidant, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer activities. Identifies mangiferin, quercetin, gallic acid, and phenolic acids as key bioactive constituents.
research.reference: Ediriweera MK, Tennekoon KH, Samarakoon SR. Evid Based Complement Alternat Med. 2017. DOI: 10.1155/2017/6949805

comparisonTraits.leaf: Long, lanceolate, dark green, glossy leaves with prominent midrib; 15–45 cm long
comparisonTraits.flower: Small, pale yellow-pink flowers in large panicles (up to 60 cm long)
comparisonTraits.stem: Tall, evergreen tree up to 30–40 meters with dense canopy; thick, rough, dark gray bark
comparisonTraits.smell: Sweet, fruity aroma from flowers and ripe fruit; leaves have a mild resinous scent

name: Guyabano (TL)
shortDescription: Isang tropikal na puno ng prutas kung saan ang mga dahon at buto ay nagtataglay ng malalakas na sangkap na may napatunayang katangiang laban sa kanser, pamamaga, at mikrobyo.

preparation.description: Boil 5–10 dried or fresh guyabano leaves in 2 cups of water for 15 minutes. Strain and drink warm, 1 cup 2–3 times daily.
Blend ripe guyabano fruit flesh and drink as juice. Rich in vitamin C, fiber, and natural sugars.
Crush fresh leaves into a paste and apply to the affected area.

facts.origin: Central America, Caribbean, and northern South America; cultivated worldwide in tropics
facts.habitat: Tropical lowlands; thrives in warm, humid environments at sea level to 1,500 m elevation

warnings: Consult a doctor before using for medicinal purposes, especially for cancer.
Guyabano leaf tea is not a substitute for professional cancer treatment.
Excessive consumption of seeds may be neurotoxic (linked to atypical Parkinsonism in some studies).
Avoid use during pregnancy; may cause uterine contractions.
Do not exceed recommended doses; consult healthcare professional for long-term use.
Not a substitute for chemotherapy or prescribed cancer treatment.

cultivationGuide.soil: Deep, well-drained, sandy or loamy soil with good organic matter
cultivationGuide.sunlight: Full sun (6–8 hours daily); tolerates partial shade when young
cultivationGuide.watering: Regular watering; prefers consistent moisture but not waterlogged
cultivationGuide.growthTime: 3–5 years from seed to bear fruit; 2–3 years from grafted tree
tips: Protect from strong winds.
Mulch around the base to retain moisture.
Hand-pollinate flowers for better fruit set.
Harvest fruit when spines begin to separate and color changes to yellowish-green.

research.title: A Review on Annona muricata and Its Anticancer Activity
research.summary: Comprehensive review (cited 124 times) focusing on A. muricata extract's role against various types of cancer, modulation of cellular proliferation and necrosis, and bioactive compounds responsible for anticancer effects. Confirms that acetogenins selectively target cancer cells while sparing normal cells, making it a promising complementary cancer therapy.
research.reference: Ilango S, Sahoo DK, Paital B, Kathirvel K, Gabriel JI. Cancers (MDPI). 2022;14(18):4539. DOI: 10.3390/cancers14184539. PMC9497149

research.title: Anticancer Properties of Graviola (Annona muricata): A Comprehensive Scientific Review
research.summary: Review (cited 262 times) summarizing the current understanding of anticancer effects of A. muricata and its constituents on diverse cancer types. Acetogenins inhibit mitochondrial complex I, selectively targeting ATP-deficient cancer cells. Activity confirmed against breast, prostate, lung, colon, pancreatic, and leukemia cell lines.
research.reference: Radi I, Nair JJ, Che CT, Abbasi AH, Chowdhury S, Akhtar MS. J Exp Pharmacol. 2018;10:115–127. DOI: 10.2147/JEP.S169645. PMC6091294

research.title: Potential Benefits of Annona muricata in Combating Cancer: A Review
research.summary: Review (cited 127 times) exploring A. muricata as a potential complementary cancer treatment agent. Documents anticancer mechanisms including induction of apoptosis, inhibition of angiogenesis, and suppression of tumor growth. Confirms bioactivity across multiple cancer cell lines with acetogenins as the primary active compounds.
research.reference: Yajid AI, Ibrahim TH, Ahmad S, Zainal Abidin Z. Biomed Pharmacother. 2018;104:376–387. DOI: 10.1016/j.biopha.2018.05.074. PMC5862046

comparisonTraits.leaf: Large, oblong, glossy dark green leaves with prominent midrib; 7–20 cm long
comparisonTraits.flower: Solitary, creamy yellow-green, bell-shaped flowers with a strong fruity scent; 3–5 cm long
comparisonTraits.stem: Medium-sized tree up to 6–8 meters; dark gray bark with irregular scaly plates
comparisonTraits.smell: Flowers have a strong, sweet, fruity aroma; leaves have a mild herbal scent when crushed

name: Pansit-pansitan (TL)
shortDescription: Isang damong karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga hardin at malilim na lugar sa Pilipinas. Napatunayang mabisang lunas laban sa rayuma (anti-gout), pamamaga, at pananakit ng katawan.

preparation.description: Boil 1 handful of fresh whole plant in 2 cups of water for 10 minutes. Strain and drink warm, 1 cup 2–3 times daily.
Eat fresh leaves and stems raw as a salad vegetable.
Crush fresh leaves into a paste and apply directly to the affected area.

facts.origin: Tropical Americas; naturalized in tropical regions worldwide
facts.habitat: Shady, moist areas in gardens, lawns, and waste places in tropical regions

warnings: Consult a doctor before using for medicinal purposes.
Not a substitute for prescribed gout medication (e.g., allopurinol, colchicine).
Do not consume in excessive amounts.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women should consult a healthcare professional before use.
Ensure correct plant identification — some look-alikes may not have the same properties.

cultivationGuide.soil: Moist, rich, well-drained soil; thrives in shaded, humid conditions
cultivationGuide.sunlight: Partial shade to full shade (prefers filtered light)
cultivationGuide.watering: Keep soil consistently moist; does not tolerate drought well
tips: Grows readily in shady garden spots or between stepping stones.
Requires consistent moisture and protection from direct sun.
Harvest the whole plant when flowering for maximum potency.

research.title: Anti-inflammatory and analgesic activity of Peperomia pellucida (L.) Kunth (Piperaceae)
research.summary: Study confirmed significant anti-inflammatory (paw edema induced by carrageenin and arachidonic acid) and analgesic activity (abdominal writhes and formalin tests) of P. pellucida. Effects were dose-dependent and comparable to standard anti-inflammatory drugs. (Cited 167 times)
research.reference: de Fátima Arrigoni-Blank M, Andrade FA, Bolognese AM, Blank AF, Niculau ES, de Aquino AM. J Ethnopharmacol. 2004;91(2-3):215–218. DOI: 10.1016/j.jep.2003.12.010. PMID: 15120441

research.title: Anti-hyperuricemic and Anti-inflammatory Effects of Micropropagated Plants of Peperomia pellucida (L.) Kunth
research.summary: Study demonstrated anti-hyperuricemic activity of P. pellucida leaf extract and anti-inflammatory activity of root extract, indicating its potential as a complementary therapy for gout. (Cited 47 times)
research.reference: Rahmi EP, Rachmawati S, Rahayuningsih E, Widyasari A. Scientia Pharmaceutica. 2020;88(1):9. DOI: 10.3390/scipharm88010009. PMC7092620

research.title: The chemistry and biological activities of Peperomia pellucida (L.) Kunth (Piperaceae)
research.summary: Comprehensive review (cited 98 times) documenting the chemistry and biological activities of P. pellucida, including anti-inflammatory, analgesic, antihyperuricemic, antioxidant, antimicrobial, and antihyperglycemic properties. Key compounds include pellucidin A, a sterol derivative with potent anti-inflammatory activity.
research.reference: Alves NSF, Pereira MCR, da Costa Silva D et al. J Ethnopharmacol. 2019;236:391–408. DOI: 10.1016/j.jep.2019.02.029

comparisonTraits.leaf: Small, heart-shaped, translucent green leaves on thin, watery stems
comparisonTraits.flower: Tiny, spike-like greenish flowers (characteristic of Piperaceae); no petals
comparisonTraits.stem: Translucent, succulent, watery stems that appear almost glass-like
comparisonTraits.smell: Mild, slightly peppery scent when crushed (family Piperaceae)

name: Malunggay (TL)
shortDescription: Isang punong siksik sa nutrisyon na ang mga dahon ay mayaman sa bitamina at protina. Napatunayang may katangiang laban sa pamamaga at diabetes. Madalas itong tawaging 'miracle tree'.

preparation.description: Add fresh malunggay leaves to soups (tinola, sinigang) during the last 2–3 minutes of cooking to preserve nutrients.
Boil 1 cup of fresh or dried leaves in 2 cups of water for 10 minutes. Strain and drink warm.
Dry leaves in shade, grind into powder. Mix 1 teaspoon into food, drinks, or smoothies daily.

facts.origin: Northern India (Himalayan foothills); cultivated throughout the tropics
facts.habitat: Tropical and subtropical regions; extremely drought-tolerant

warnings: Root bark extract can be toxic in large doses — do not consume roots or bark extracts.
Pregnant women should avoid consuming root bark (may cause uterine contractions).
Consult a doctor before using for medicinal purposes.
Do not replace prescribed medications with malunggay alone.
Pregnant or breastfeeding women should consult a healthcare professional before use.

cultivationGuide.soil: Well-drained, sandy or loamy soil; tolerates poor and alkaline soil
cultivationGuide.propagation: Seeds, stem cuttings (20–30 cm cuttings root easily)
cultivationGuide.growthTime: Fast-growing; harvestable in 6–8 months from cuttings; produces pods in 6–8 months
tips: Cut back the trunk to 1 meter to encourage bushy leaf growth for leaf harvest.
Prune regularly for continuous leaf production.
Extremely resilient — survives drought, poor soil, and neglect.
Harvest leaves every 2–3 weeks for continuous supply.

research.title: Moringa oleifera: An Updated Comprehensive Review of Its Nutritional and Medicinal Properties
research.summary: Comprehensive review (cited 575 times) documenting M. oleifera's nutritional composition and medicinal properties including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antidiabetic, antimicrobial, hepatoprotective, cardioprotective, and neuroprotective activities. Confirms it as one of the cheapest and most reliable alternatives for good nutrition.
research.reference: Pareek A, Suthar M, Rathore GS, Bansal V. Nutrients. 2023;15(4):860. DOI: 10.3390/nu15040860. PMC9916933

research.title: Moringa oleifera: A review on nutritive importance and its medicinal application
research.summary: Highly cited review (cited 2,323 times) documenting that M. oleifera provides 7 times more vitamin C than oranges, 10 times more vitamin A than carrots, 2 times more protein than milk, and 4 times more calcium than milk. Confirms antioxidant, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antitumor properties.
research.reference: Gopalakrishnan L, Doriya K, Kumar DS. Food Sci Hum Wellness. 2016;5(2):49–56. DOI: 10.1016/j.fshw.2016.04.001

research.title: Moringa oleifera is a Prominent Source of Nutrients with Potential Health Benefits
research.summary: Review (cited 506 times) confirming M. oleifera as a rich source of macro- and micronutrients and bioactive compounds including flavonoids, phenolic acids, glucosinolates, and thiocarbamates. Documents antidiabetic, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and hepatoprotective properties.
research.reference: Islam Z, Fatima R, Saeed B et al. Int J Food Sci. 2021;2021:6696925. DOI: 10.1155/2021/6696925. PMC8373516

comparisonTraits.leaf: Compound leaves with small, oval leaflets arranged in pairs along a central stem; soft, green, fern-like appearance
comparisonTraits.flower: White, fragrant flowers with yellow centers in loose drooping clusters; about 2.5 cm wide
comparisonTraits.stem: Slender, fast-growing trunk with soft, light gray bark; young stems are green and flexible
comparisonTraits.smell: Mild, slightly horseradish-like scent when leaves or roots are crushed (milder than true horseradish)
